cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the wedding calls. Your date is still safe; the venue needs a little rearranging.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please tell me we still have the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We have the garden. I wanted you to have that before I told you the hall won't open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stop planning around me. Is it repairs, or has something happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There was a fire. I'll wait while you call your sister, then we'll choose somewhere together.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes planning control and A3/A5 reveal garden-only then fire, but A3 explains its disclosure technique instead of simply protecting through the choices.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 hall hope prompts A3 garden; B4 objects to being planned around; A5 chooses a sister call B has not requested.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants agency and direct facts, a plausible concern beyond eliciting another reveal.

heightening.evidence: A5 reveals fire but imposes another step rather than directly yielding the control challenged by B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 wedding date and A3 unusable hall are legible; the sister adds an unnecessary relationship.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 wanted-you-to-have-that is a mechanism explanation and A5 sister call is a gratuitous staging choice.
